Task 0 — Create Azure Resources & Foundry

Set up the resource group, Key Vault, and Azure AI Foundry project that your workload will use.

🏗️ Why create a dedicated resource group?
Grouping your Key Vault and Foundry resource together means you can apply RBAC, tags, and lifecycle policies in one place. In production, every AI workload environment should live in its own resource group — easier to audit, easier to delete cleanly.
🤖 What is Azure AI Foundry?
Azure AI Foundry (formerly Azure Machine Learning Studio) is the hub for deploying and managing AI models. When your app calls Azure AI APIs, it's typically hitting a Foundry resource endpoint. This is why the app identity needs RBAC access here.
1
Navigate to portal.azure.com and sign in. Search for and select Resource groups, then click + Create.
2
Enter rg-foundry-lab as the resource group name, select your region, then select Review + create → Create.
3
Search for and select Key vaults from the Azure portal search bar.
4
Click + Create. Select the rg-foundry-lab resource group, enter a globally unique Key Vault name, then click Review + create → Create.
5
Once the Key Vault is deployed, open ai.azure.com and click Start Building. Sign in with your Azure credentials.
6
Create a project when prompted. Expand Advanced options and set: Foundry resource name (unique), Subscription, Resource group → rg-foundry-lab, Region → any AI Foundry recommended region. Click Create.
📝If prompted with "All set. Let's build your agents", click "Let's go" to continue.
✅ Resource group, Key Vault, and Azure AI Foundry project are deployed and ready.

Task 1 — Add API Permissions for the Application

Grant the Contoso-AI-App permission to read user profiles from Microsoft Graph without user interaction.

🔑 API permissions vs RBAC roles — what's the difference?
API permissions control what data your app can reach through APIs like Microsoft Graph. RBAC roles control access to Azure infrastructure like storage, Key Vault, or AI services. Most AI workloads need both — Graph permissions for user data, RBAC for resource access.
⚠️ Why does User.Read.All require admin consent?
Application-level permissions (not delegated) are high-privilege — they don't involve a signed-in user, so the app acts on its own behalf across all users. Microsoft requires a Global Administrator to explicitly approve these before the permission activates. This is a security checkpoint by design.
1
Navigate to entra.microsoft.com. Under Entra ID, select App registrations, then select Contoso-AI-App. In the left sidebar, select API permissions.
2
Click + Add a permission.
3
On the Request API permissions flyout, select Microsoft Graph.
4
Select Application permissions (not Delegated). Search for User.Read.All and check the box, then click Add permissions.
5
Back on the API permissions page, verify User.Read.All appears under Microsoft Graph with status Not granted for lab Directory.
📝Not granted is expected here — admin consent is required in production before this permission activates. The lab doesn't grant consent, so this status is correct.
✅ API permission configured. Contoso-AI-App can now request Graph access once an admin grants consent.

Task 2 — Grant Access to the Foundry Resource

Assign the Cognitive Services User RBAC role so the app can call AI inference endpoints.

🛡️ What is the Cognitive Services User role?
This role grants read-access to AI model endpoints and inference APIs on the Foundry resource. It lets the service principal call the AI model without being able to manage or delete the resource itself. Always use least-privilege — never Owner or Contributor for a workload account.
1
In the Azure portal, navigate to Resource groups → rg-foundry-lab. Select the resource with type Foundry.
2
Select Access control (IAM) from the left panel, then click + Add → Add role assignment. Under Job function roles, search for and select Cognitive Services User.
3
Click Next. On the Members tab, select User, group, or service principal → + Select members. Search for Contoso-AI-App, select it, then click Select → Next → Review + assign.
💡You should see a blue notification at the top right confirming the role assignment was added successfully.
✅ Contoso-AI-App can now call AI inference endpoints on the Foundry resource.

Task 3 — Grant Access to Key Vault

Assign the Key Vault Secrets User role so the app can read secrets without full vault access.

🔐 Key Vault Secrets User vs Key Vault Reader
Secrets User can read secret values. Reader can only see the vault's metadata — it cannot retrieve the actual secret content. AI workloads that load API keys or connection strings from Key Vault need Secrets User, not just Reader.
1
Navigate back to rg-foundry-lab and select the Key vault resource. Select Access control (IAM) → + Add → Add role assignment.
2
Under Job function roles, search for and select Key Vault Secrets User.
3
Click Next. On the Members tab, select User, group, or service principal → + Select members. Search for Contoso-AI-App, select it, then click Select → Next → Review + assign.
⚠️Key Vault access model must be set to Azure RBAC (not access policies) for role assignments to work. Confirm this under your Key Vault's Access configuration blade.
✅ You've successfully granted the application read access to secrets in Azure Key Vault.
🎉

Exercise Complete!

The Contoso-AI-App identity now has scoped, least-privilege access to every resource it needs — Graph API, AI Foundry, and Key Vault.
